surprises.description: TRU reported adjusted EPS of $1.25, $0.04 above the high end of its Q3 guidance and above the preview’s $1.23–$1.25 whisper range. The result was stronger than the preview’s published-consensus ceiling of $1.21.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS rising 14% to $1.25, beating the high end of guidance by $0.04.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The buy-side whisper is almost certainly $1.23–$1.25”; consensus EPS was “$1.19–$1.21.”

surprises.description: Rather than holding or cutting FY EPS guidance as the preview’s base case contemplated, TRU raised its outlook to 12%–13% growth, or $4.81–$4.88. That is above the prior $4.75–$4.83 range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted diluted EPS guidance was raised 1 percentage point to 12%-13% growth ($4.81-$4.88).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case said “FY EPS range maintained via cost offsets,” while its key question was whether guidance would be “held at $4.75–$4.83, or cut?”

surprises.description: The margin outlook deteriorated more than the preview’s margin-acceleration case implied: underlying margins are now expected to be flat to up 20 bps, versus the prior expectation of 50–70 bps of expansion. TRU cited technology reinvestment and higher legal and regulatory costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted EBITDA margin is guided down 60-80 basis points, with underlying margins now expected flat to up 20 bps (versus prior 50-70 bps expansion) due to reinvestment in technology and higher legal/regulatory costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the margin guide embedded “+20–40bps underlying expansion” and expected Q4 to be “the margin-acceleration quarter.”

surprises.description: Mortgage inquiries fell 16% in Q3, and the outlook worsened further: full-year inquiries are now expected to decline about 10%, with a decline of more than 20% in Q4. That is weaker than the preview’s mid-to-high-single-digit full-year decline assumption and its low-double-digit H2 inquiry assumption.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Despite a 16% decline in inquiries, with full-year mortgage inquiries now expected to decline ~10% and more than 20% in Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the mortgage guide assumed “mid-to-high-single-digit FY inquiry declines” and TRU had guided Q3 assuming “only low-double-digit H2 inquiry declines.”

surprises.description: Mortgage revenue growth came in below the preview’s referenced Q3 guide, both reported and excluding FICO royalties: 21% versus 28% reported, and 5% versus 6% ex-FICO. The reported growth was still strong, but missed those benchmarks.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the guide assumed mortgage growth of “+28% reported (+6% ex-FICO royalty).”

surprises.description: TRU provided a more specific and bounded estimate of bi-merge exposure: a shift from tri-merge to bi-merge would affect about $33 million of revenue and $0.15 of adjusted EPS, below 1% of revenue and under 3% of EPS. This narrows the preview’s broader roughly $100 million-plus at-risk framing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Only ~$100 million in annual revenue is directly tied to the FHFA Tri-Merge requirement, with a shift to bi-merge impacting roughly $33 million in revenue and $0.15 of adjusted EPS—less than 1% of revenue and under 3% of EPS.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described “~$100M+” of revenue tied to GSE tri-merge and said a quantified, bounded bi-merge impact was important; its bull case anticipated “<2% revenue.”

surprises.description: TRU’s organic constant-currency growth was 8%, above the preview’s Q3 guidance range of 4.0%–5.5%. Excluding FICO mortgage royalties, growth was 5.5%, at the top of that range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 organic constant currency revenue grew 8% (5.5% excluding FICO mortgage royalties).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q3 organic constant-currency growth guidance of “+4.0% – +5.5%.”

surprises.description: The balance sheet and buyback plans improved beyond the preview’s starting point: leverage fell from the cited 2.6x to 2.5x, and the buyback authorization increased by $1 billion to $2 billion, with about $500 million of repurchases planned for the year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reduced its leverage ratio to 2.5x, reaching the top of its long-term target range, and increased buyback authorization by $1 billion to $2 billion while planning ~$500 million in full-year repurchases.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “leverage 2.6x vs. <2.5x target” and “$150M repurchased YTD with H2 ‘at least comparable.’”

surprises.description: International growth returned to double digits, with India and Latin America each growing 18%; India’s reported growth was well above the preview’s cited 8%. Some Brazil growth was one-time revenue, tempering the quality of the regional result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “International returned to double-digit growth at 10%, led by India and Latin America each growing 18%, though some Brazil growth was one-time revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “India +8%, Canada +10%, Mexico ahead of plan” as part of the non-mortgage growth setup.

surprises.description: TRU disclosed an additional 2027 earnings headwind not raised in the preview: net interest expense is expected to rise by roughly $60 million, partly because a 1.4% swap expires and is replaced with one in the mid-4% range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “2027 net interest expense is expected to rise by roughly $60 million due to higher rate forecasts and replacement of an expiring 1.4% swap with a new swap in the mid-4% range.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed that VantageScore was used in roughly 35% of mortgage credit pulls in Q3, providing a concrete adoption measure that the preview did not give. The preview had flagged VantageScore pricing as a potential bi-merge mitigation, but did not state an expected usage level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “VantageScore was included in roughly 35% of mortgage credit pulls in Q3.”

surprises.description: TRU said Insurance is expected to exceed $430 million in 2026 revenue and has reached a scale comparable to mortgage revenue excluding FICO royalties. The preview provided no Insurance-specific revenue outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Insurance delivered its ninth straight quarter of double-digit growth and is expected to exceed $430 million in 2026 revenue, now comparable to the mortgage business excluding FICO royalties.”
